what_changed: OCC, Federal Reserve, FDIC and NCUA propose new third-party risk management guidance (comments due November 16, 2026) that, if finalized, would replace the 2023 Interagency Guidance on Third-Party Relationships (88 FR 37920) and the supplemental resources (OCC Bulletin 2002-16, the 2024 bank-fintech deposit statement, and the 2024 community bank guide). It reorganizes TPRM into four components (sec. B): risk identification and assessment (relationship inventory, risk identification, risk assessment); risk oversight (due diligence and selection, contract negotiation, ongoing monitoring, termination); residual risk acceptance; and governance. It extends to insured credit unions, tailors oversight to assessed risk rather than 'critical activities', defines a third-party relationship as a business arrangement typically under a written agreement, says subcontractors alone do not create a direct oversight presumption, states the guidance is non-enforceable and that deviation alone will not be a basis for supervisory action, and notes consumer compliance considerations are not directly addressed.
compliant_agent_must_now: No change until final. If finalized, bank and credit union clients would scale due diligence, contract terms and ongoing monitoring of an AI servicing provider to their own risk assessment of that relationship; a servicing agent that talks to borrowers, handles payments or data is likely to be assessed as higher risk. The provider should be ready to supply evidence proportionate to that assessment (controls, incident history, compliance testing, subcontractor list), and register row TPRM-001 would need its citation updated once the 2023 guidance is rescinded.
open_questions_for_deploying_team: Which clients are supervised by which agency, and how will their risk tiering of the servicing relationship change their due-diligence requests?
Does the servicing provider use subcontractors (e.g., model or telephony providers) that clients may still ask to see, even though the proposal removes the presumption of direct oversight?
TPRM-001 is marked 'verify cite'; this document confirms the 2023 guidance citation 88 FR 37920 (June 9, 2023).
rationale: Full text confirms proposed interagency guidance on how banks and credit unions examine third parties, directly within the vendor-examination part of the test.
